_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); machinery and engines signals

pit_profile.why: 'Caterpillar is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives' (FY2016 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and product support services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical and can be significantly reduced in periods of economic weakness characterized by lower levels of government and business investment, lower levels of business confidence, lower corporate earnings, perceived or actual industry overcapacity, higher unemployment and lower consumer spending.', 'The energy and mining industries are major users of our products, including the coal, iron ore, gold, copper, oil and natural gas industries.' and 'Changes in environmental and climate change laws or regulations, including laws relating to greenhouse gas emissions, could lead to new or additional investment in product designs and could increase environmental compliance expenditures.' (Item 1A): the 10-K calls the demand for its own products cyclical (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical'), so CYCLICAL from the FY2010 10-K; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, which a maker of construction and mining equipment, engines and turbines does not hold, so the climate-change wording stays here

classification.quality_note: 'Caterpillar is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives' (FY2016 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and product support services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical and can be significantly reduced in periods of economic weakness characterized by lower levels of government and business investment, lower levels of business confidence, lower corporate earnings, perceived or actual industry overcapacity, higher unemployment and lower consumer spending.', 'The energy and mining industries are major users of our products, including the coal, iron ore, gold, copper, oil and natural gas industries.' and 'Changes in environmental and climate change laws or regulations, including laws relating to greenhouse gas emissions, could lead to new or additional investment in product designs and could increase environmental compliance expenditures.' (Item 1A): the 10-K calls the demand for its own products cyclical (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical'), so CYCLICAL from the FY2010 10-K; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, which a maker of construction and mining equipment, engines and turbines does not hold, so the climate-change wording stays here. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 14.73x; +102% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.62; conservative 2yr -19%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -61.5%/yr (worst year FY07-FY16, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +13.0%/yr (FY17 guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +13.0%/yr (FY07-FY16 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +43.4%/yr (best 2-yr run FY07-FY16); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: CAT (retrospective, 2017-09-15) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 14.73x (92.6% downside to Bear $9 / +6.3% upside to Bull $129) | Adj composite 2.55 vs market 3.17: gap -0.62 [OVERVALUED] | +102% above the EPP floor $60 (12x FY17E $5.00) | Conservative 2-yr case: -18.6% total (-9.3%/yr) | At 24.3x FY17E the 15% hurdle price $161 sits above the BULL case; Machinery sales +13.7% in Q2 2017, forward revenues +9-14.2% (FY17 sales and revenues guide); ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining; no theme in scope has dated evidence.

sources.title: Caterpillar FY2016 10-K
sources.supports: 2012-2016 sales and revenues and profit per share - diluted (five-year summary), 2014-2016 statement of results, 2015-2016 external sales by segment, 2016 cash, operating cash flow and dividends; Items 1 and 1A

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: fourth-quarter 2016 results release
sources.supports: fourth-quarter 2016 sales and revenues by segment and statement of results, full-year 2016 actuals and adjusted profit per share for 2016 and 2015; 2017 outlook: sales and revenues $36 to $39 billion, adjusted profit about $2.90 per share (about $2.30 including restructuring costs)

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: first-quarter 2017 results release
sources.supports: first-quarter 2017 sales and revenues by segment and statement of results; 2017 outlook: sales and revenues $38 to $41 billion, profit about $3.75 per share excluding restructuring costs (about $2.10 including them)

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: second-quarter 2017 results release
sources.supports: second-quarter 2017 sales and revenues by segment and statement of results; 2017 outlook: sales and revenues $42 to $44 billion, adjusted profit about $5.00 per share (about $3.50 including restructuring costs and the IronPlanet gain)

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: third-quarter 2016 results release
sources.supports: third-quarter 2016 sales and revenues by segment and statement of results; 2016 outlook: sales and revenues about $39 billion, profit $3.25 per share excluding restructuring costs ($2.35 including them); preliminary 2017 sales and revenues not significantly different

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: 'Caterpillar Splits Stock; Increases Dividend Rate'
sources.supports: a two-for-one stock split; the split shares distributed on July 13 to stockholders of record on June 22, 2005
